note: refactor-cpu-core phase 2. The whole-chip numbers T4/T5/T8 ask for do NOT exist: the design cannot be placed, because its 64 KB main memory is modelled as an on-chip array (rtl/ram_async.sv) with no memory abstraction behind it. See docs/cpu-core.md.

target.target_freq_status: aspirational: rtl/pll.v is generated for 50 MHz but rtl/top.sv never instantiates it, so the board runs the raw 25 MHz pin

whole_chip.measured: 2026-07-25, after the PPU agent guarded ram_async's $display dumps behind `ifdef VERILATOR` (a $display reading mem[] is an async read port to yosys, which blocked BRAM inference) and temporarily shrank the main RAM to 8 KB via RAM_ADDR_BITS=13
whole_chip.yosys: completes in 45 s and emits 7,869 SB_LUT4 and 48 SB_RAM40_4K
whole_chip.reading: The CPU is 720 of 7,869 LUT4 - 9% of the design. The PSG is 5,044, or 64%. Removing the main RAM's 16 blocks (add-memory-subsystem) brings BRAM to exactly 32/32; logic would still be 139% over. Logic, not memory, is the harder capacity problem, and the CPU is not where it lives.
whole_chip.note_t8: T8 asked whether the CPU's area crowds out the remaining ISA slices. At 9% of the design it does not; the question is whether anything fits at all.

core_only.harness: rtl/cpu_fmax_top.sv: one core plus a 2 KB synchronous-read RAM with ram_async's timing. No memory arbiter, so a difference between runs is a difference between cores.

arlet.critical_path: starts at a registered decode signal (V) -> store -> write_back -> inc -> index_y -> dst_reg -> regfile -> ALU half-carry -> PC. 11.75 ns logic.

v2.critical_path: after phase 4: starts at the memory read data but ends at the state register - RDATA -> di -> decode table -> next state. The ALU and flag paths now start at the registered decode row, not at DI.

core_only.note_seeds: Fmax varies with the placement seed; three seeds are reported so a 2% difference is not read as a result.

throughput.note: static mean CPI over Breakout's 1,928 instructions

other_clock_consumers.psg: rate derived from the CLK_HZ parameter (chip.sv:22, top.sv:22); clock-portable, no benefit
other_clock_consumers.lcd_serialiser: runs at the system clock, so a faster clock is a shorter frame push - the one part that gains
other_clock_consumers.compositor: per-line cycle budget scales with the clock

psg_register_reads.evidence: rtl/psg.sv CPU-interface block only assigns dout; no register read alters sequencer or channel state. So the corpus's one indexed MMIO site (sta PSG_CH,y at src/main.asm:2479) is safe against a spurious read.

phase4.change: registered the decode row (dec_r); implied/accumulator instructions moved to their own state; added a data-bus hold register so a stall cannot destroy a pending read
